part.text:
All done. Here's what was implemented in `ringbuf.c`:

- **`rb_create`** — allocates opaque struct with a `count` field to avoid head==tail ambiguity when full
- **`rb_destroy`** — frees both the struct and its buffer (NULL-safe)
- **`rb_write`** — writes up to `len` bytes, wrapping at buffer boundary; returns actual count written
- **`rb_read`** — reads oldest bytes first with wrap-around; decrements count
- **`rb_peek`** — copies from tail without advancing pointers
- **`rb_size` / `rb_capacity`** — return `count` and `capacity` respectively
- **`rb_clear`** — resets head, tail, and count to zero

All functions are NULL-safe per the spec. Compiled cleanly with `gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Werror` and all tests pass.
